A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, Figures 1–6, and Appendices A–G. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: Section 4.3 reports original synthetic ICL simulations and an English/German sentiment experiment using the Multilingual Amazon Reviews Corpus. Appendix G reports additional per-source simulation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic experiments, multilingual sentiment experiment, and per-source results in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Both versions use linear attention with a two-layer nonlinear MLP, one gradient step on the first layer, and second-layer ridge regression on fresh data. The initialization-dimension correction aligns with the already specified shape of F rather than introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian-mixture nonlinear regression settings and English/German Amazon review sentiment task. No datasets, languages, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the linear Transformer, nonlinear MLP Transformer, and equivalent polynomial model. Figures 2–6 retain the same Transformer-versus-equivalent-model comparisons.

E3.justification: The source-averaged squared-error metric, experimental dimensions, sample and context sizes, activation choices, regularization, and preprocessing remain unchanged. The revised input-mean bound is a theoretical assumption, not a reported change to the experiments.

E4.justification: The same analyses vary sample size, context length, hidden dimension, covariance structure, noise, mixing ratios, and gradient step size. Appendix G retains identical per-source analyses.

E5.justification: Both report averages over 20 Monte Carlo runs for the synthetic experiments and 100 trials for the multilingual experiment. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 1–6 are identical, including Appendix G. No numerical results or result entries are added, removed, or replaced; the empirical trends remain the same.

T1.justification: The supporting theory is substantively revised. Assumption 4.2 tightens the squared input-mean norm bound from O(d) to O(d^(1/2)), and Lemma 4.9 removes the almost-sure convergence qualification. Appendix B corrects normalization and replaces Cov(b) with E[bb^T] in concentration and covariance calculations. Lemma C.3 changes two bounds from tilde-O(k^(1/2)) to tilde-O(1) and from tilde-O(1) to tilde-O(k^(-1/2)), with a revised conditioning argument. Appendix C restricts beta to (0,1) and explicitly states eta=o(k^beta); Appendix D now invokes eta times the residual norm tending to zero. These changes affect assumptions and reasoning supporting the central equivalence theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same main contributions: polynomial equivalence, benefits of nonlinear MLPs, the influence of data quality and mixing, and the importance of task structure for feature learning.

C2.justification: Section 4.3.5 qualifies the English-data interpretation: a higher English proportion now 'can lead' to improved performance, replacing the earlier unqualified wording. The tighter input-mean assumption also narrows theoretical applicability, while the other mechanism explanations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: The source-code link, experimental hyperparameters, training details, and multilingual-e5-small embedding, PCA, and normalization instructions are retained. No new implementation, hardware, runtime, or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The same 47 references are retained, and the related-work discussion preserves the same positioning relative to linear-attention ICL, nonlinear MLP studies, and Gaussian universality.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar corrections, standardizes norm notation, revises several proof explanations, and adds a funding acknowledgment. The overall narrative and section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive limited caption and notation edits, including the context-length symbol in Figure 1. Spacing and some appendix page breaks change, but all six figures retain their plots, axes, legends, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through the second-moment correction in Appendix B, revised conditioning and rate arguments in Appendix C, and clearer convergence and residual-scaling statements. These repairs make the existing equivalence argument more internally consistent. The tighter input-mean assumption reduces formal generality, while the central contributions and empirical evidence remain unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
